process.title: From “where do I start?” to “taken care of.”
process.text: Know what comes next, at every step.

steps.label: Connect
steps.title: Tell us your situation.
steps.text: Choose a service, book an office visit, or start remotely. We'll define the scope and confirm the fee.

steps.label: Prepare
steps.title: Bring it all together.
steps.text: Gather the relevant documents. We review the information and follow up on what's missing.

steps.label: Move forward
steps.title: Review. Approve. File.
steps.text: Review the prepared work and authorize the filing. Leave with a clearer understanding of your next steps.

faq.title: A little clarity, before you start.

personal-tax.name: Personal tax
personal-tax.intro: From your first return to retirement, get personal tax help that sees the whole picture. In person in Vancouver and Burnaby, or remotely across Canada.

image.alt: An accountant reviewing tax documents with a couple in a bright office

scope.title: A return that reflects your real life.
scope.text: A new job. A first home. A growing family. We help you understand what to bring and what happens next.

items.title: Income, brought together
items.text: Employment, pensions, investments, rental income, and self-employment in one coordinated return.

items.title: Credits worth a closer look
items.text: A review of the deductions and credits relevant to your circumstances, including tuition, medical expenses, donations, and RRSP contributions.

items.title: Changes handled thoughtfully
items.text: Support with prior-year returns, adjustments, moving, retirement, and changes in family circumstances.

docs: Photo identification and prior-year notice of assessment
Employment, pension, investment, and other income slips
RRSP receipts and relevant deduction receipts
Rental or self-employment records, if applicable
Details of changes in address, residency, or family status

faqs.question: Can I file without visiting an office?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start through the existing remote filing page, or contact us to discuss the best way to share your documents.

faqs.question: Can you help with more than one tax year?
faqs.answer: Tell us which years you need prepared. We will review the scope and confirm the records required and fees before proceeding.

faqs.question: How much will my return cost?
faqs.answer: Your fee depends on the income sources and work involved. Contact us for a quote tailored to your situation.

corporate-tax.name: Corporate tax
corporate-tax.intro: Corporate tax preparation and year-end support for Canadian business owners. Connect your records, your corporate return, and your next business decision.

image.alt: Business owners reviewing a financial report with an accountant

scope.title: A more connected year end.
scope.text: Bookkeeping, business tax, and your personal return belong in the same conversation. Start with where your business is today.

items.title: Corporate returns
items.text: T2 return preparation and a review of the supporting financial information and schedules required for your corporation.

items.title: Owner-manager coordination
items.text: Review salary and dividend considerations alongside your corporate and personal tax needs.

items.title: Year-end readiness
items.text: Identify missing records, reconcile key balances, and coordinate bookkeeping, GST/HST, and payroll needs.

docs: Prior corporate tax return and notice of assessment
Year-end trial balance, general ledger, and financial statements
Bank, credit card, loan, and investment statements
Asset purchases, disposals, and financing details
Shareholder, payroll, dividend, and GST/HST records

faqs.question: Is this different from filing as a sole proprietor?
faqs.answer: Yes. A corporation files a corporate return. Sole-proprietor income is generally addressed through a personal return. Tell us how your business is structured so we can direct you.

faqs.question: Can you help if my books are behind?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can discuss catch-up bookkeeping and the work needed to prepare your records for the corporate return.

faqs.question: Can you coordinate my personal and corporate tax?
faqs.answer: We can review both engagements together so owner compensation and supporting records are considered consistently.

bookkeeping.name: Bookkeeping
bookkeeping.intro: Organized records and a clearer view of your numbers. Monthly bookkeeping, catch-up support, and year-end coordination for Canadian businesses.

image.alt: Calculator and colour-coded documents on a desk

scope.title: Find the right level of support.
scope.text: Choose ongoing monthly help, a one-time cleanup, or bookkeeping coordinated with year-end tax. We will quote the work your business needs.

items.title: Monthly bookkeeping
items.text: Transaction categorization, bank and credit card reconciliations, and organized financial records.

items.title: Catch-up and cleanup
items.text: Bring outstanding months into order and identify missing information before year end.

items.title: Connected business support
items.text: Discuss payroll, GST/HST reporting, QuickBooks support, and corporate tax as part of a clearly defined service plan.

docs: Business structure and current bookkeeping software
Months or years requiring bookkeeping
Bank, credit card, and payment processor statements
Sales invoices, purchase receipts, and expense records
Payroll, loan, and GST/HST records, if applicable

faqs.question: Can you work with QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell us which version you use and how your current records are maintained so we can discuss the setup and access required.

faqs.question: Do you offer catch-up bookkeeping?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share the outstanding periods and approximate transaction volume so we can assess the work and provide a quote.

faqs.question: What does monthly bookkeeping cost?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on transaction volume, the number of accounts, record quality, and the services included. We confirm your scope and fee before work starts.

pace.title: Support at your pace.
pace.note: Each engagement is quoted to your transaction volume, records, and service scope.

items.label: Ongoing
items.title: Monthly support
items.text: Keep reconciliations and records current, month after month.

items.label: A fresh start
items.title: Catch-up & cleanup
items.text: Get outstanding periods organized and ready for the next step.

items.label: Connected
items.title: Books + year end
items.text: Coordinate bookkeeping with corporate tax and year-end preparation.

trust-estate-tax.name: Trust & estate
trust-estate-tax.intro: Tax preparation support for executors, trustees, and families. Make sense of the records, returns, and next steps with a clear, considered approach.

image.alt: Small model house with a coin

scope.title: A clear place to begin.
scope.text: You do not need to have every answer before you speak with us. Start with the documents available and we will help organize the next steps.

items.title: Final personal returns
items.text: Review the deceased person’s tax records and discuss the final personal return and other returns that may be relevant.

items.title: Estate and trust returns
items.text: T3 return preparation, beneficiary reporting, and supporting schedules based on the trust or estate circumstances.

items.title: Executor and trustee support
items.text: Organize the information needed for the engagement and discuss outstanding returns, tax notices, and clearance certificate support.

docs: Date of death and executor or trustee contact details
Will, trust deed, and relevant legal documents
Prior returns, tax notices, and trust account details
Income slips and investment statements
Asset values, disposition records, and distribution details

faqs.question: Is the final personal return the same as an estate return?
faqs.answer: They are separate filings. We review the income, dates, and estate activity to identify the returns that may be needed.

faqs.question: Can I start before I have all the documents?
faqs.answer: Yes. A consultation can help you identify the missing records and plan the next steps.

faqs.question: Do all estates and trusts need the same forms?
faqs.answer: No. Requirements depend on the type of trust or estate and its circumstances. We confirm the preparation scope after reviewing the details.
